title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Stockport £30,000 per annum + study + benefits

Join a successful manufacturing business where your contribution really counts.

Are you an organised, detail-oriented finance professional looking for your next opportunity within a supportive team? This is a great opportunity to join an established packaging business in Stockport, as an Accounts Assistant, supporting the day-to-day running of the finance function.

Reporting directly to the Finance Manager, you ll play an important role in keeping financial records accurate, ensuring transactions are processed efficiently and helping the business maintain effective financial controls.

This is a varied, hands-on position offering the opportunity to build on your existing accounts experience, develop your skills and gain broader exposure to the finance function.

The role

Working closely with the Finance Manager and wider business, your responsibilities will include:
- Processing purchase invoices and credit notes, ensuring accurate coding, supporting documentation and approvals.
- Maintaining customer and supplier accounts and allocating receipts and payments.
- Completing bank reconciliations and investigating discrepancies or unreconciled transactions.
- Supporting credit control by monitoring outstanding balances, issuing statements and following up overdue invoices.
- Checking employee expenses and maintaining petty cash records.
- Assisting with month-end activities, including ledger checks, accruals, prepayments and supporting schedules.
- Providing financial information for VAT returns, audits and management reporting.
- Responding to customer and supplier queries professionally and helping resolve issues promptly.
- Maintaining accurate, organised and confidential financial records.
- Identifying opportunities to improve routine processes and supporting the wider finance team as required.

About you

You ll be numerate, methodical and comfortable working with financial information, with a strong eye for detail and a proactive approach to getting things done.

We re looking for someone with:
- A good understanding of basic bookkeeping and purchase and sales ledger processes.
- Strong numerical skills and a high level of accuracy.
- Confidence using Microsoft Excel, including basic formulas, sorting and filtering.
- Good organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks and meet deadlines.
- Clear communication skills and a professional approach to customer and supplier queries.
- The ability to work independently on routine tasks while contributing positively to a team.
- A responsible approach to confidentiality and sensitive financial information.

Previous experience in an accounts, bookkeeping or finance administration role would be advantageous. AAT qualified, studying towards AAT, or equivalent practical experience would also be welcomed.

Experience with bank reconciliations, credit control, month-end processes or accounting software would be beneficial, although a willingness to learn is just as important.

What s on offer?
- £30,000 annual salary plus benefits
- The opportunity to join an established business.
- A varied role with exposure to several areas of finance.
- Direct support and development from the Finance Manager.
- The opportunity to strengthen your accounting skills and develop your experience within a busy finance function.

Interested?

If you re looking for a hands-on Accounts Assistant role where you can make a valuable contribution, build your experience and become part of a supportive finance team, we d love to hear from you.

Apply today to find out more.

title: Office Administrator
description:
At OFG Education we put wellbeing first by giving our teams more time to recharge

Job Title: Office Administrator
Location: Brinksway School, Stockport, SK4 2 HG
Hours: 40 hours per week Monday to Friday 8.00am - 4.00pm
Salary: £25,000.00 per annum (not pro rata)
Contract: Permanent Term Time Only
Start: December 2026
UK applicants only - no sponsorship available

About the Role

We are a warm and welcoming small SEN school and are looking for an experienced administrator to deal with parent enquiries and administrative tasks in the school office. This is a varied and rewarding role where you will be at the heart of the operation, ensuring the smooth day-to-day running of the office while supporting colleagues, service users, families, and external professionals.

As the first point of contact for visitors, calls, and enquiries, you will create a professional and welcoming environment while managing a wide range of administrative responsibilities. You will play a key role in maintaining accurate records, coordinating admissions and reviews, supporting recruitment and HR processes, assisting with financial administration, and ensuring compliance with regulatory and safeguarding requirements.

Key responsibilities include:
- Providing efficient and confidential administrative support to managers and colleagues.
- Managing reception duties, including answering calls, welcoming visitors, handling post, and coordinating meeting rooms.
- Maintaining accurate records, databases, files, and documentation in line with company policies and data protection requirements.
- Supporting referral, assessment, admission, review, and discharge processes.
- Coordinating meetings, preparing documentation, and taking accurate minutes where required.
- Assisting with recruitment administration, staff records, onboarding, DBS checks, attendance monitoring, and HR documentation.
- Supporting the administration and organisation of examinations and qualifications processes.
- Assisting with financial administration, including petty cash, invoices, expense claims, purchasing, and budget tracking.
- Coordinating facilities administration, maintenance requests, vehicle records, and asset registers.
- Supporting compliance, safeguarding, health and safety, and regulatory reporting requirements.
- Working collaboratively with colleagues to ensure a responsive and efficient administrative service.

About You

We are looking for a highly organised and professional administrator who can manage a varied workload, prioritise effectively, and maintain the highest levels of accuracy and confidentiality.

You will be confident communicating with a wide range of people, from colleagues and managers to families, visitors, and external agencies. Able to work both independently and as part of a team, you will be proactive, adaptable, and committed to delivering excellent administrative support.

You will have:
- Previous experience in an administrative or office support role.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Good IT skills, including experience using Microsoft Office and database systems.
- The ability to produce accurate correspondence, reports, letters, and records.
- Experience handling sensitive and confidential information with discretion.
- A flexible and positive approach to supporting a busy service environment.
- The ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively.

Above all, you will be a reliable and dedicated professional who takes pride in providing exceptional administrative support and contributing positively to the success of the service.

About Us

At OFG Education, we believe every student deserves an education designed around who they are. Through high expectations, deep expertise and truly personalised education, we help students realise their potential and prepare for successful futures.

Building on more than 20 years of experience, we are bringing our approach to more students and communities around the world. Across the UK, Iberia and the Gulf, our schools combine the strength, expertise and high standards of an international education group with the individuality of each school and the communities they serve.

Whatever your role, joining OFG Education means contributing to our shared ambition: empowering every student to success through truly personalised education.

About Our School

Opened in September 2024, Brinksway School is a purpose-built Primary and Secondary SEN school for 55 students aged 4-13 with autism and complex needs. Located in Stockport, Greater Manchester, our refurbished, specialist building supports learning, independence, and wellbeing.

At Brinksway School, we passionately nurture each student's potential. Our curriculum is tailored to individual needs, aiming not only for academic success but also for growth in confidence, self-esteem, and life skills. We aspire to create a positive, inclusive, and stimulating environment where every student feels valued, supported, and inspired to flourish.

We are proud to be a part of OFG Education who in 2025 were officially certified as a 'Great Place to Work' for the sixth year running.

Why Join Us?

We place students and vulnerable young adults at the heart of everything we do, so every day brings the satisfaction of making a real difference. We are committed to the safeguarding and promoting the welfare of students and young people. All applicants will be subject to social media checks and successful applicants to a fully enhanced DBS.
- Life Assurance
- Pension scheme with options to increase contributions
- "Your Wellbeing Matters" - mental health support and physical health checks
- Flexible Benefits Platform (Vista), including:
- Health, wellbeing and insurance benefits
- Hundreds of UK and international discounts
- Cycle to Work Scheme & Electric Car Purchase Scheme
- Critical illness cover
- Family Growth Support, including enhanced maternity/paternity leave and paid fertility treatment support

We reserve the right to close the vacancy early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications.

OFG Education is committed to carrying out a fair, thorough and efficient recruitment process in line with Keeping Children Safe in Education. Whilst we aim to keep applicants informed throughout, OFG Education does not accept liability for any loss of earnings or other associated costs incurred by applicants as a result of delays or changes in the compliance process. All stages of the compliance process are subject to necessary safeguarding checks and compliance with statutory requirements, which may affect timescales.

title: Operations Administrator
description:
Your new company
You will be joining a growing international technology business based in Stockport. Due to continued expansion, the company is strengthening its Operations team and creating a new opportunity for someone looking to develop their experience in order fulfilment, logistics and supply chain operations.
Your new role
As Operations Administrator, you will play an important role in ensuring orders, freight movements and system information remain accurate and up to date.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Monitoring inbound and outbound freight movements, identifying delays, revised delivery times or customs issues
- Creating and maintaining Sales Orders and Purchase Orders
- Updating supplier ETAs, stock receipt dates and customer order despatch dates
- Liaising with suppliers, carriers and freight forwarders for updates
- Arranging courier and freight collections
- Preparing shipping documentation and maintaining import and export files
- Keeping internal teams informed through accurate system updates
- Supporting the Warehouse with collections, priorities and expected stock movements
- Escalating delays, customs issues and non-standard shipments where required

What you'll need to succeed
You will be organised, dependable and confident, managing several orders or shipments at once. Strong attention to detail, clear communication skills and a proactive approach are essential.
Previous experience in administration and customer service is essential, although transferable skills will also be considered. You should be comfortable using Microsoft Office and spreadsheets, with experience of an ERP or order management system advantageous but not essential.
What you'll get in return
You will receive a salary of 27,000 - 29,500 depending on experience. This is a varied role offering hands-on exposure to international freight, order fulfilment, supplier management, shipping documentation and customs processes. As your knowledge and confidence develop, you will have the opportunity to take on greater responsibility within the Operations team.

title: Part time Payroll Specialist
description:
Part-Time Payroll Specialist
Location: Didsbury, South Manchester
Hours: 25-30 hours per week over 5 days
Salary: Up to £35,000 FTE, plus bonus
Working pattern: Hybrid - 3 days in office, 2 days WFH

Client Details

In this role, you'll be responsible for coordinating the full UK payroll process. You'll play a key role in ensuring payroll is accurate, compliant and delivered on time, working closely with HR, Finance and external payroll providers.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership of payroll operations, maintaining strong controls and identifying opportunities to improve processes. With part-time hours and a flexible hybrid working approach, we recognise the importance of finding the right balance between work and life outside the office.

Description

The key responsibilities of a Part time Payroll Specialist will be:
- Manage the end-to-end monthly UK payroll process, including data preparation, calculations, employee payments, payslips and statutory submissions.
- Ensure all payroll activities comply with UK legislation, including PAYE, National Insurance, RTI reporting, statutory payments and workplace pension obligations.
- Oversee outsourced payroll processing across four international countries, ensuring accurate data, timely approvals, appropriate funding and compliance with local regulations.
- Complete payroll reconciliations and investigate variances, providing accurate payroll data and insights to support the Finance team.
- Partner with HR to manage employee lifecycle changes, including new starters, leavers, salary adjustments, contractual changes, absences and benefits.
- Maintain effective payroll controls and accurate records, ensuring clear audit trails, appropriate documentation and robust approval processes across UK and international payrolls.
- Coordinate payroll year-end processes, support audits and system updates, and manage relationships with external payroll providers.
- Review existing payroll processes and implement improvements to enhance accuracy, efficiency and overall service delivery.
- Act as a key point of contact for payroll queries, resolving issues promptly and providing clear, reliable support to employees and internal stakeholders.

Profile

A successful Part time Payroll Specialist will have:
- Previous experience managing or coordinating an in-house UK payroll.
- Good knowledge of UK payroll legislation, including HMRC and pension requirements.
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage deadlines effectively.
- Experience working collaboratively with Finance, HR and external payroll providers.
- The ability to investigate and resolve payroll queries confidently.
- Strong communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
- The ability to handle confidential information with discretion and professionalism.

Job Offer
- Salary: Up to £35,000 FTE, pro rata + bonus
- Hybrid working: 3 days in the office, 2 days working from home
- Pension: Salary sacrifice scheme.
- Life assurance
- Enhanced sick pay: Company sick pay scheme.
- Private medical insurance: Single cover, with option to add family.
- Annual leave: 25 days plus bank holidays.
- Extra holiday: Option to buy up to 10 additional days.
- Additional paid leave for key occasions.
- Birthday day off.
- Enhanced parental leave
- Free on-site parking

title: Post Appointment Insolvency Administrator
description:
Post-Appointment Corporate Insolvency Administrator

Location: Stockport

Working arrangements: Hybrid

Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience

Develop your corporate insolvency career with a specialist firm offering varied casework and hybrid working.

Imperium Financial Recruitment is recruiting a Post-Appointment Corporate Insolvency Administrator to join a firm of Insolvency Specialists based in Stockport.

This opportunity would suit someone with practical corporate insolvency experience who enjoys taking responsibility for case progression, resolving queries and working with a range of stakeholders.

You will focus on the administration of corporate insolvency cases following appointment, working closely with Insolvency Practitioners and senior colleagues to progress assignments through to closure.

The role

Your responsibilities will include:
- Managing an allocated portfolio of post-appointment corporate insolvency cases under appropriate supervision.
- Preparing statutory reports, notices, correspondence and supporting case documentation.
- Liaising with directors, creditors, solicitors, agents, accountants and other relevant parties.
- Gathering and reviewing company books, records and financial information.
- Assisting with the identification, protection and realisation of company assets.
- Supporting investigations into company affairs and highlighting matters requiring further review.
- Reviewing creditor claims and assisting with distributions.
- Monitoring statutory deadlines and following up on outstanding actions.
- Maintaining accurate case records and updating the case management system.
- Liaising with the cashiering team regarding receipts, payments and account reconciliations.
- Providing clear progress updates to managers and Insolvency Practitioners.
- Preparing cases for closure and ensuring outstanding matters are addressed.

About you

Previous experience in corporate insolvency administration, including post-appointment casework, is essential.

You will also bring:
- A working knowledge of corporate insolvency procedures, particularly Creditors' Voluntary Liquidations.
- Experience progressing cases and preparing accurate documentation.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing deadlines.
- Clear written and verbal communication skills.
- Confidence dealing professionally with directors, creditors and external advisers.
- A proactive approach to resolving queries and moving cases forward.
- Good attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining complete case files.
- The ability to work independently within your experience level and seek guidance when needed.

A relevant insolvency qualification, such as the CPI, would be advantageous but is not essential where suitable practical experience can be demonstrated.

The opportunity
- Hybrid working, combining time at home with attendance at the Stockport office.
- A dedicated focus on post-appointment corporate insolvency work.
- Exposure to varied cases within a specialist practice.
- The opportunity to build your technical knowledge alongside experienced insolvency professionals.
- Scope to take on greater case responsibility as your experience develops.
